_notice: Every figure, citation, deadline and authority name in this file was drafted
by a developer from secondary sources and has NOT been reviewed by anyone
qualified to confirm it. It must not be demoed to a real tenant or used to
generate a letter until a human has checked each field against the primary
`lastReviewedAt` is deliberately ABSENT rather than filled in with today's
date. Its absence is the signal (R9): the UI omits the 'rules last reviewed'
line when it is missing, so an unreviewed table cannot masquerade as a
reviewed one. Adding the date is the act of taking responsibility for the
contents, and only a human can do that.
architecture.md §9.2 and the demo-safety skill: statutory references,
deadlines, authority names and interest figures come from this table and from
code, NEVER from a model. That rule exists because a model will produce
confident, plausible, wrong law. It applies to how this file was written as
much as to how it is read.
_mtaAdopted_note: Karnataka had not notified the Model Tenancy Act 2021 as state law at the time of drafting. VERIFY: a state that has since adopted it changes the deposit cap and the forum.
_depositCapMonths_note: The Karnataka Rent Act 1999 is the operative statute and, unlike the MTA's 2-month residential cap, does not impose a general cap that is reliably enforced in practice; Bengaluru market practice is commonly 6-10 months. 0 encodes 'no statutory cap asserted' and must not be displayed as 'the cap is zero'. VERIFY before any UI copy depends on it.
_refundWindowDays_note: No statutory refund window is asserted here. 30 days is the common contractual term and is used as the default clock only where the tenancy agreement is silent. VERIFY: this drives the refund deadline printed in a demand letter, so a wrong number here is the R9 failure the review date exists to surface.
_statutoryInterestBps_note: Integer basis points (600 bps = 6.00% per annum). 0 encodes 'no statutory interest rate asserted for Karnataka'. The claim arithmetic must treat 0 as 'no interest claim', never as a rate to multiply by.
_authorityName_note: VERIFY the correct forum and its current name before this appears in a letter.

escalationSteps.label: Written demand to the landlord
escalationSteps.description: Send a dated, itemised demand for the deposit, attaching the condition report and the move-out comparison. Keep proof of delivery.

escalationSteps.label: Legal notice
escalationSteps.description: A formal notice through an advocate, restating the demand and a deadline to pay. Many disputes settle at this step.

escalationSteps.label: Civil suit for recovery
escalationSteps.description: A suit for recovery of the deposit. Small-value claims may be filed in the Court of Small Causes. Consult an advocate about forum, limitation and court fees.
